Device health

One card per appliance with a single health badge rolled up from harvest, cache age, deep monitors and capacity — each problem explained underneath — plus an on-demand hardware scan over SSH.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view appliances.edit
📍 WhereMonitoring → Fleet health → Device health (URL /monitoring/), in every ADOM

What is it?#

Device health answers one question per appliance: is this device still there and in good shape? Each appliance gets a card with one badge — healthy, warning, critical or unknown — and every signal that is not healthy is written under the badge, so a state is never unexplained. The page reads only SATOM's own data; loading it never contacts an appliance.

What does it do?#

  • Rolls four signals into one status per appliance. The worst signal wins, and unknown never counts as healthy:
Signal (label on the card) ok warning critical unknown
Harvest — the last five configuration harvests the latest one succeeded the latest failed (fewer than 3 in a row) 3 or more failed in a row never harvested
Cache — age of the newest cached configuration younger than the cache budget (6 h by default) nothing cached, or older than the budget older than 4× the budget —
Deep monitors — the device's enabled deep monitors all ok a probe warns or could not run, or all probes are disabled a probe is critical no monitors, never run, or all suppressed
Capacity — object counts against the admin cap within the thresholds over the warning % over the critical % no admin cap set
  • Lists health problems and capacity problems as alert lines at the top (up to 8 of each).
  • Shows per appliance: kind, model, firmware, HA mode, hardware (vCPU, RAM, disk), a maintenance marker, the capacity bars, and how fresh the cached data is.
  • Shows Device HA posture: per appliance, what the harvested configuration says about HA (clustered, standalone or unknown), with the members and their roles.
  • Collects hardware facts on demand with Scan hardware (SSH).
  • Refreshes itself every 30 seconds.

Requirements#

  • Appliances registered under Appliances.
  • Something that harvests them. A harvest is a full read of the device's configuration into SATOM's cache. It is written by:
  • the scheduled action Sync device to local source of truth (or Sync device + push SoT off-box);
  • a Discovery / Rediscovery (recorded with trigger rediscovery);
  • SATOM itself after an approved change is written to a device.
  • Deep monitors and capacity limits, if you want those two signals graded. See Deep monitors and Capacity limits.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the page and its data The legacy view permission, which any granular view key grants (for example appliances.view). Each user sees the appliances of the current ADOM, and maintenance devices only with appliances.view_maintenance.
Scan hardware (SSH) appliances.edit or appliances.apply (legacy config_write; any other edit/apply permission also unlocks it). Offered in the Global and FortiWeb ADOMs only.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the page and its data now require a view permission; signing in alone is no longer enough. Each card is now graded with its own product's capacity and cache limits, like the alert engine, and the hardware scan only targets FortiWeb appliances.

🔑Permission — Without the permission

A user without any view permission gets 403 Forbidden on the page. The Scan hardware (SSH) button is not shown to users without an edit/apply permission, nor in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs, where there is nothing it can scan.

How to use#

Read the page#

  1. Open Monitoring → Fleet health → Device health. In the Global ADOM the subtitle links to SATOM health, the installation's own health page.
  2. Read the alert lines at the top first: critical before warning.
  3. On each card, the badge is the overall status; the lines under the capacity bars name each signal that is not ok, for example Harvest harvest failing (3 runs in a row) - ….
  4. The top right shows when the page last refreshed and the global capacity thresholds: updated 10:42:05 · warn ≥ 80% · crit ≥ 95%. Each card is graded with its own product's thresholds, which can differ from these (see Configuration). Refresh reloads immediately.

Understand "never harvested" hints#

SATOM creates the harvest schedule (device_sync) with its default System Automations when the node gets its first appliance, and only if the node has no System Automation yet; until then, or after the row was deleted or disabled, no harvest schedule covers the device. A card then says Harvest never harvested and Cache no cached configuration on this node — that is not a device fault. When SATOM can see that no enabled schedule covers the device, it says so and gives the command:

never harvested - no 'device_sync' schedule on this node (run: sudo satom execute seed actions --yes)

The same hint appears for Deep monitors when no deep_monitor schedule exists (probes have never run - no 'deep_monitor' schedule on this node …).

To fix it:

  1. Either run a Rediscovery of the device now — it fills the cache as a harvest — or
  2. create the schedules: run sudo satom execute seed actions --yes on the node, or add a Sync device to local source of truth action under Scheduled actions.
  3. Click Refresh.

Scan hardware (SSH)#

Discovery and harvests read the configuration over REST; they do not collect CPU, memory or disk sizes. Those come from a read-only SSH battery of FortiWeb commands, so the scan covers FortiWeb appliances only:

  1. Click Scan hardware (SSH). The button changes to Scanning…, then Scanning in the background….
  2. SATOM opens one SSH session per FortiWeb appliance visible in the current ADOM and runs get system status, diagnose hardware cpu list, diagnose hardware mem list, diagnose hardware harddisk list and diagnose hardware logdisk info.
  3. When it finishes, the cards show n vCPU · n GB RAM · n GB disk.

The scan is a background job (Hardware scan — fleet). It stays silent when every device was scanned. If some devices failed, you get a warning notification naming them; if all failed, the job ends in error and you get an error notification. A device that could not be scanned keeps its previous hardware data.

A card without hardware data reads no hardware inventory — use “Scan hardware (SSH)” above; rediscovery does not collect it.

Configuration#

Setting Description Default
Cache budget (stale_hours) Age after which the cached configuration counts as stale. Per product on the Thresholds settings page, falling back to the global monitoring.stale_hours. 6 h
Critical multiplier (crit_stale_mult) Cache older than budget × this is critical 4
Harvest error streak (error_streak_crit) Failed harvests in a row that make the signal critical 3
Capacity warning / critical % Thresholds for the capacity bars. Per product on the Thresholds settings page, falling back to the global capacity.warn_pct / capacity.crit_pct. 80 / 95

See Settings for the Thresholds page.

Example#

🧪Example — A device that went away

fweb-02 was powered off on Monday. On Tuesday its card reads critical:

  • Harvest — harvest failing (5 runs in a row) - device refused the sweep (310 endpoints failed, 0 objects) — cache kept. First error: …
  • Cache — cache 1 d old (budget 6 h)

The configuration pages keep serving Monday's cache: a harvest in which the device returned nothing never overwrites the last good cache.

Result#

  • The page itself changes nothing.
  • Scan hardware (SSH) stores one hardware record per appliance (CPU count and model, memory, disks, and the raw command output). The Architecture map reads the same record.

Troubleshooting#

Every card says "unknown"#

Possible causes — Nothing has been harvested, no deep monitors exist and no capacity caps are set. Unknown means "not measured", not "broken".

Solution — Harvest the devices (see Understand "never harvested" hints above), configure deep monitors and capacity caps as needed.

Verification — After a harvest the Harvest and Cache lines disappear from the card (they are ok).

"Deep monitors: N/M probes alerting" on a device that looks healthy#

Possible causes — Server-policy probes created before 2026-10-14 that point at VIPs SATOM cannot reach. Their result reads unreachable: ConnectTimeout or ConnectError, while CPU, memory and proxyd are ok. When the list is long, the line names four probes and adds "(+N more)".

Solution — On Deep monitors, disable those probes, or make the VIPs routable from SATOM. Probes discovered from 2026-10-14 on are created disabled in this case.

Verification — The card's deep-monitor line reads "N probes ok".

"No deep monitors configured" on a device that was just added#

Possible causes — The device was added less than 3 minutes ago through a path that the next Collection sweep covers, or it is in maintenance.

Solution — Wait for the next sweep or run Discover from device → Device baseline. A device in maintenance gets no probes until it leaves maintenance.

Verification — The line changes to "N probes have never run", then to "N probes ok" after the first deep-monitor pass.

"harvest failing (n runs in a row) - device refused the sweep (… endpoints failed, 0 objects) — cache kept."#

Possible causes — The device answered no request at all: down, licence-locked, wrong credentials, or a TLS failure.

Solution — Run Test Connection on the appliance's page, then a Rediscovery to see per-endpoint errors.

"all 3 deep monitors disabled - no coverage"#

Possible causes — Every deep monitor bound to the device is switched off. A disabled probe is reported as lost coverage, never as a passing check.

Solution — Re-enable the monitors in Deep monitors, or remove them if the device no longer needs them.

"no admin caps set (4 object types)"#

Possible causes — No capacity catalog with a cap exists for this model and firmware.

Solution — Set the hard max or operational cap under Capacity limits.

"hardware scan failed on every device: …"#

Possible causes — SSH is closed on the devices, or the credentials do not work over SSH.

Solution — Check SSH from the Operator console.

"no visible FortiWeb appliance to scan (the hardware scan is FortiWeb-only)"#

Possible causes — The current ADOM shows no FortiWeb appliance. The scan's command battery is written for FortiWeb only.

Solution — Switch to the FortiWeb or Global ADOM. Other products show no hardware data on their cards.

Advanced#

Advanced One grading for the page and the alerts

The page and the alert engine use the same roll-up code and the same per-product limits (cache budget, critical multiplier, harvest error streak, capacity warning and critical %), so a device the page shows as critical is the device the alert mail is about. Deep monitors that are suppressed keep running and keep their own status, but stop speaking for the device; they are reported as lost coverage.

Advanced Which cached layer counts

The cache signal reads the newest of the device's cached layers: the configuration layer (harvest) and, on FortiWeb, the deep layer (deep capture). Products without a deep layer are graded on the configuration layer alone.
